\looseness=-1 All experiments use proprioceptive observations; pixel and multi-modal inputs remain untested. The evaluation is limited to simulated environments and does not include real robot transfer. Our compute budget (${\sim}80$ GPU hours on a single GPU) restricts the scale of the factorial design; larger sweeps may reveal additional interaction effects. Seed counts of four to five per condition provide sufficient power for binary CIVO classification but may not capture fine-grained effect sizes across all environmental conditions.

\paragraph{Environment Complexity Dependence.} CIVO onset exhibits a non-monotonic relationship with environment complexity. Across six DeepMind Control Suite tasks spanning 1 to 21 degrees of freedom (DoF), CIVO occurs exclusively in 6-DoF environments: Walker Walk (3/5 seeds, 60\%) and Cheetah Run (3/4 seeds, 75\%). Lower-DoF environments do not trigger the phenomenon. In Cartpole Swingup (1 DoF), the gate degrades performance through non-value-driven mechanisms (NVE $< 0.1\times$); the single-joint dynamics appear too simple for value overestimation to cascade through learned temporal embeddings. In Hopper Hop (4 DoF), the gate causes transient learning delay followed by recovery to 85\% of baseline performance after extended training (168K steps vs.\ the standard 105K evaluation window), though this observation rests on a single seed ($n{=}1$) and warrants replication. At higher DoF, a different obstacle emerges. Both Quadruped Walk (12 DoF) and Humanoid Walk (21 DoF) baselines exhibit intrinsic value overestimation (NVE $= 6.6\times$ at 125K steps and $12.97\times$, respectively) without any gate mechanism. These failures stem from known scaling challenges of DreamerV3 in high-dimensional action spaces~\citep{hafner2025dreamerv3} and preclude clean isolation of gate-induced CIVO from pre-existing overestimation. Our empirical characterization of CIVO is therefore grounded in 6-DoF moderate-complexity locomotion, and whether the onset boundary extends to higher DoF remains contingent on achieving stable baselines in those regimes.
tool_args.new_string: \looseness=-1 All experiments use proprioceptive observations; pixel and multi-modal inputs remain untested. The evaluation is limited to simulated environments and does not include real robot transfer. Our compute budget (${\sim}80$ GPU-hours on a single GPU) restricts the scale of the factorial design; larger sweeps may reveal additional interaction effects. CIVO has been characterized in moderate-complexity locomotion (6-DoF); higher-DoF baselines exhibit intrinsic value overestimation~\citep{hafner2025dreamerv3} that precludes clean isolation, and lower-DoF environments do not trigger the phenomenon, leaving the exact complexity boundary open.

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{F6: $\dt{=}1$ imagination eliminates CIVO.}
Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding (exp\_008e\_v3; Appendix~\ref{sec:code_corrections}) yields 0/4 CIVO (peak NVE ${\leq}0.8\times$); three seeds achieve $65$--$96\%$ of baseline (mean $775.6$; Figure~\ref{fig:multiple_pathways}). The trained embedding still receives gradients and develops $\dt$-conditioned representations, but since imagination exclusively queries $\dt{=}1$, the critic never encounters the biased $\dt{>}1$ predictions where reward fidelity degrades (\S\ref{sec:f2}). This localizes the vulnerability: the temporal embedding is necessary for co-adaptation, but the value amplification pathway requires $\dt{>}1$ rollouts to propagate bias into the critic. Multi-step imagination, not the trained embedding alone, is the necessary trigger for CIVO onset.

\paragraph{F7: Full-pathway gradient stopping shows mixed results.}
\looseness=-1 Full-SGS (exp\_018) detaches all non-KL gradients from $e_{\dt}$. Seed~1 shows partial mitigation (eval 448.3, NVE $1.66\times$) with late instability (NVE rising from $1.23\times$ mean to $1.66\times$ at 95K), suggesting SGS delays onset rather than prevents it; seed~2 collapses entirely (peak ${\sim}488$ at 75K $\to$ 40.8 at 105K), matching the untreated pattern despite gradient blocking (Appendix~\ref{sec:sgs_gradient_analysis}). The seed divergence indicates that full-SGS creates a metastable regime where stochastic factors determine whether the delayed onset crosses a critical threshold within the training horizon. Cross-environment validation on Cheetah confirms CIVO generalization (010b, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$); full-SGS yields 0/3 elimination. Removing the embedding eliminates CIVO on Cheetah (024b, NVE $< 0.2\times$). Targeted obs-decoder-only SGS (exp\_025/026) achieves 1/6 prevention (1/4 Walker, 0/2 Cheetah; Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}), confirming pathway redundancy: even with the dominant gradient channel blocked (the observation decoder), the remaining KL pathway provides sufficient learning signal for co-adapted representations that eventually amplify into value overestimation (Appendix~\ref{sec:seed_divergence}).
